title: THE CITY BURNED, THE FAMILY LIVES

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then they burned the whole city and everything in it, but they put the silver and gold and the articles of bronze and iron into the treasury of the Lord's house. But Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, with her family and all who belonged to her, because she hid the men Joshua had sent as spies to Jericho — and she lives among the Israelites to this day. — Josh 6:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two outcomes stand side by side in these verses. The city of Jericho is burned to the ground, given over completely to God's judgment. And Rahab, with her whole family, is not only spared but comes to live among the people of God — "she lives among the Israelites to this day." The outsider becomes an insider. The condemned becomes a member of God's own people.

This is a stunning picture of what grace does. Rahab did not merely escape destruction; she was brought all the way in, adopted into the community of God's people, given a home and a future among them. That is the fullness of salvation. God does not just rescue us from judgment; He brings us into His family and gives us a place among His own.

The silver and gold going into "the treasury of the Lord's house" reminds us that everything ultimately belongs to God. But the far greater treasure God gained that day was Rahab herself — a soul brought from a pagan city into the fellowship of His people.

This is exactly what God does for every believer in Christ. We were once "foreigners and strangers," but through Christ we are brought near and made "members of God's household" (Eph 2:19). Like Rahab, we do not deserve it; we simply trust the God who saves. And He does not leave us on the outside. He brings us home, to live among His people, now and forever.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you grasp that salvation is not just rescue from judgment but adoption into God's family?
2. How does Rahab's move from outsider to insider mirror your own story in Christ?
3. Are you helping other "outsiders" find their place among God's people?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in Christ You not only spared me but brought me into Your family. Help me welcome others as You have welcomed me. Amen.
